hints.title: Ordered Query Processing
hints.text: Sort queries in ascending order along with intervals sorted by start point to process points monotonically.

hints.title: Active Intervals by Length
hints.text: Maintain active intervals containing the query point ordered by interval length (right - left + 1).

hints.title: Pruning Expired Intervals
hints.text: Discard intervals from consideration whose end points are strictly smaller than the current query coordinate.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def minInterval(self, intervals: list[list[int]], queries: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        intervals.sort()
        sorted_queries = sorted([(q, i) for i, q in enumerate(queries)])

        pq = []
        ans = [-1] * len(queries)
        idx = 0
        n = len(intervals)

        for q, orig_idx in sorted_queries:
            while idx < n and intervals[idx][0] <= q:
                l, r = intervals[idx]
                heapq.heappush(pq, (r - l + 1, r))
                idx += 1

            while pq and pq[0][1] < q:
                heapq.heappop(pq)

            if pq:
                ans[orig_idx] = pq[0][0]

        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(n log n + q log q)
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all n intervals for each of q queries takes O(n * q) time, which exceeds limits for 10^5 elements.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual sorting and priority queue pruning evaluates active intervals in O((n + q) log n) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate sorts queries and intervals, using a min-heap on interval length with lazy expiration.

solutions.approach: Sorted query line sweep with min-heap for shortest active interval
